function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: Generates a Dockerfile in the specified repository directory with a default configuration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the repository directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory name within the filesystem.

base_image.description: The base image to use in the Dockerfile. For example, 'python:3.8-slim'.

maintainer.description: The maintainer information to be added to the Dockerfile. Format should be 'Name <email@example.com>'.

port.description: The port number that the container will expose. For example, '80' for a web server.

commands.description: Additional commands to be executed when building the image, separated by ';'. For example, 'apt-get update; apt-get install -y git'.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be a valid path relative to the project root.

deployment_name.description: The name to assign to the Kubernetes deployment. This name must be unique within the Kubernetes namespace.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to use for the deployment. This should include the repository name and tag, if applicable, in the format 'repository/image:tag'.

replicas.description: The number of instances to deploy for the specified Docker image.

service_type.description: The type of service to create for the deployment. Typical values include 'ClusterIP', 'NodePort', and 'LoadBalancer'.

port.description: The port number that the service should expose. This should correspond to the port that the application inside the Docker container is set to listen on.

target_port.description: The target port on the pod to which the service will send requests. This should be the same as the port that the application inside the Docker container is set to listen on.

function.name: analyse_repo_contents
function.description: Analyzes the contents of a repository to determine the predominant programming language used within. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the repository is located. This should be the root directory of the repository.

include_subdirectories.description: A flag indicating whether to include subdirectories in the analysis. If set to true, all subdirectories will be recursively analyzed.

excluded_files.description: An array of file names or patterns to exclude from the analysis, such as ['README.md', '*.txt'].

language_threshold.description: The percentage threshold for a language to be considered predominant in the repository. This should be a value between 0 and 100. This is a float type value.

message.content:
Below is a practical “recipe” you can follow (or copy‑paste into your own scripts) to get everything up and running.  
I’ll walk through each step, give you the exact commands you’d run locally, and supply the template files that will be generated automatically.  

> **NOTE** – I’m not able to actually clone or push to the remote repository from here, so the instructions assume you’re working on a machine that has `git`, `docker`, `kubectl`, and `jq` installed and that you have SSH access to the repo (`git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`).  

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the Repository

```bash
# Make sure you have an SSH key added to your GitHub account
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"   # skip if you already have one
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

# Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

If you prefer HTTPS:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the Repo & Generate Artifacts

### 2.1 Detect the Predominant Language

Run this quick script (you can paste it into a file called `detect_lang.sh` and execute it):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Count lines per language using cloc
cloc --json . > cloc.json

# Extract the language with the highest line count
predominant=$(jq -r '.languages | to_entries[] | select(.value.code == (.value.code | max)) | .key' cloc.json)

echo "Predominant language: $predominant"
```

> **Prerequisite:** Install `cloc` (`sudo apt install cloc`) and `jq` (`sudo apt install jq`).

### 2.2 Create a Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` at the repo root with the following content (adjust the base image if you want something other than Alpine):

```dockerfile
# Use official Node.js LTS image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set metadata
LABEL maintainer="Your Name <you@example.com>"
EXPOSE 3000

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Build (if needed)
RUN npm run build || true

# Start the app
CMD ["npm", "start"]
```

> **Why this config?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is lightweight yet fully featured.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees reproducible installs.  
> * `npm run build || true` allows projects without a build step to still work.  

### 2.3 Generate Kubernetes YAMLs

Create a folder called `k8s` and add two files: `deployment.yaml` and `service.yaml`.

#### `k8s/deployment.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
```

#### `k8s/service.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What changed?**  
> * `replicas: 3` gives you basic horizontal scaling.  
> * `LoadBalancer` exposes the app externally (works on most cloud providers).  
> * Adjust `image:` to point to your registry/tag once you build/push the image.

### 2.4 Add a GitHub Actions Workflow

Create `.github/workflows/build.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version-file: .nvmrc   # or specify a version like '18.x'

    - name: Cache NPM modules
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.npm
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-node-

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci

    - name: Run tests
      run: npm test

    - name: Build Docker image
      run: |
        docker build -t zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} .
        echo "${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}" | docker login -u ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }} --password-stdin
        docker push zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}

    - name: Deploy to Kubernetes
      env:
        KUBE_CONFIG_DATA: ${{ secrets.KUBE_CONFIG_DATA }}
      run: |
        echo "$KUBE_CONFIG_DATA" | base64 --decode > kubeconfig
        export KUBECONFIG=$PWD/kubeconfig
        kubectl apply -f k8s/
```

> **Secrets required**  
> * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` & `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – to push images.  
> * `KUBE_CONFIG_DATA` – Base64‑encoded kubeconfig for your cluster.  

---

## 3️⃣ Stage All New Files

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/build.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & Push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

Once pushed, the GitHub Actions pipeline will kick off automatically, build the Docker image, push it to Docker Hub, and deploy the updated manifests to your cluster.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Dockerfile (Node.js + Alpine) |
| ✅ | `k8s/deployment.yaml` (3 replicas) |
| ✅ | `k8s/service.yaml` (LoadBalancer) |
| ✅ | GitHub Actions workflow (build, test, push, deploy) |
| ✅ | Added to git, committed, pushed |

Feel free to tweak the numbers (replicas, ports, image tags) to suit your environment. Happy coding!
